sanskrit: hiraṇyagarbhaḥ sam avartatāgre bhūtasya jātaḥ patir eka āsīt | sa dādhāra pṛthivīṁ dyām utemāṁ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
english: Hiraṇyagarbha arose in the beginning; born, he was the one lord of all that exists. He sustained this earth and yonder heaven. To which god shall we render worship with oblation?

sanskrit: ya ātmadā baladā yasya viśva upāsate praśiṣaṁ yasya devāḥ | yasya chāyāmṛtaṁ yasya mṛtyuḥ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
english: He who gives breath, who gives strength, whose command all things obey, whose command even the gods obey — he whose shadow is immortality and whose shadow is death. To which god shall we render worship with oblation?

sanskrit: yaḥ prāṇato nimiṣato mahitvaika id rājā jagato babhūva | ya īśe asya dvipadaś catuṣpadaḥ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
english: He who, by his might, became the sole king of every breathing, every winking thing — he who is lord of this two-footed and four-footed world. To which god shall we render worship with oblation?

sanskrit: yasyeme himavanto mahitvā yasya samudraṁ rasayā sahāhuḥ | yasyemāḥ pradiśo yasya bāhū kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
english: He whose greatness these snow-capped mountains proclaim, whose they say the ocean is, together with Rasā — whose are these four directions, whose are the arms. To which god shall we render worship with oblation?

sanskrit: yena dyaur ugrā pṛthivī ca dṛḻhā yena svaḥ stabhitaṁ yena nākaḥ | yo antarikṣe rajaso vimānaḥ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
english: By whom the awesome sky and the earth were made firm, by whom heaven was propped up and the vault of light — who is the measurer of the midspace. To which god shall we render worship with oblation?

sanskrit: yaṁ krandasī avasā tastabhāne abhy aikṣetām manasā rejamāne | yatrādhi sūra udito vibhāti kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
english: To whom the two armies trembling in mind looked up for help, propped up by his aid — above whom the sun shines when it has risen. To which god shall we render worship with oblation?

sanskrit: āpo ha yad bṛhatīr viśvam āyan garbhaṁ dadhānā janayantīr agnim | tato devānāṁ sam avartatāsur ekaḥ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
english: When the mighty waters came, bearing the universal germ, generating Agni — from that was born the one breath of the gods. To which god shall we render worship with oblation?

sanskrit: yaś cid āpo mahinā paryapaśyad dakṣaṁ dadhānā janayantīr yajñam | yo deveṣv adhi deva eka āsīt kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
english: He who by his power looked over the waters as they held creative force and generated sacrifice — he who was the one god above the gods. To which god shall we render worship with oblation?

sanskrit: mā no hiṁsīj janitā yaḥ pṛthivyā yo vā divaṁ satyadharmā jajāna | yaś cāpaś candrā bṛhatīr jajāna kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
english: May he not harm us — the father who brought forth the earth, who, upholding truth, generated the sky, and who generated the bright, mighty waters. To which god shall we render worship with oblation?

sanskrit: prajāpate na tvad etāny anyo viśvā jātāni pari tā babhūva | yatkāmās te juhumas tan no astu vayaṁ syāma patayo rayīṇām ||
english: O Prajāpati, none other than you has encompassed all these born beings. May whatever desire of ours we invoke you for be granted; may we become lords of riches.

sanskrit: vasuṁ na citramahasaṁ gṛṇīṣe vāmaṁ śevam atithim adviṣeṇyam | sa rāsate śurudho viśvadhāyaso 'gnir hotā gṛhapatiḥ suvīryam ||
english: I praise him who is like a good treasure, of wondrous greatness — the pleasant, auspicious, inoffensive guest. He, Agni the hotar, the householder, the sustainer of all, bestows on the devout the gift of heroic strength.

sanskrit: juṣāṇo agne prati harya me vaco viśvāni vidvān vayunāni sukrato | ghṛtanirṇig brahmaṇe gātum eraya tava devā ajanayann anu vratam ||
english: O Agni, of wise will, pleased, accept and love my words, you who know all the ways. Clothed in ghee, open the path of prayer; the gods followed after your ordinance.

sanskrit: sapta dhāmāni pariyann amartyo dāśad dāśuṣe sukṛte māmahasva | suvīreṇa rayiṇāgne svābhuvā yas ta ānaṭ samidhā taṁ juṣasva ||
english: The immortal one, traversing the seven stations, bestows on the generous, the pious — be gracious to us. With wealth that brings good heroes, O Agni, self-existent, be pleased with him who has served you with fuel.

sanskrit: yajñasya ketum prathamam purohitaṁ haviṣmanta īḻate sapta vājinam | śṛṇvantam agniṁ ghṛtapṛṣṭham ukṣaṇam pṛṇantaṁ devam pṛṇate suvīryam ||
english: Those with oblations praise the foremost ensign of sacrifice, the purohita, the seven-powered. Agni who listens, whose back is anointed with ghee, the bull, the god who satisfies — bestows heroic strength on the giver.

sanskrit: tvaṁ dūtaḥ prathamo vareṇyaḥ sa hūyamāno amṛtāya matsva | tvām marjayan maruto dāśuṣo gṛhe tvāṁ stomebhir bhṛgavo vi rurucuḥ ||
english: You are the first and most excellent messenger; invoked, rejoice for immortality's sake. The Maruts purified you in the house of the generous worshipper; the Bhṛgus made you shine bright with their praises.

sanskrit: iṣaṁ duhan sudughāṁ viśvadhāyasaṁ yajñapriye yajamānāya sukrato | agne ghṛtasnus trir ṛtāni dīdyad vartir yajñam pariyan sukratūyase ||
english: Milking refreshment from the easily milked cow that nourishes all, O sacrifice-loving Agni of wise will, for the sacrificer — dripping ghee, shining thrice through the ritual seasons, going round the sacrifice, you seek wisdom.

sanskrit: tvām id asyā uṣaso vyuṣṭiṣu dūtaṁ kṛṇvānā ayajanta mānuṣāḥ | tvāṁ devā mahayāyyāya vāvṛdhur ājyam agne nimṛjanto adhvare ||
english: You alone, at the shining forth of this Dawn, men making you their messenger have worshipped. The gods increased you, worthy of great praise, anointing you with ghee at the sacrifice.

sanskrit: ni tvā vasiṣṭhā ahvanta vājinaṁ gṛṇanto agne vidatheṣu vedhasaḥ | rāyas poṣaṁ yajamāneṣu dhāraya yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: The Vasiṣṭhas called you down, O swift one, praising you, O Agni, wise ones, at the assemblies. Establish the flourishing of wealth among the sacrificers. You gods, ever guard us with your blessings.

sanskrit: ayaṁ venaś codayat pṛśnigarbhā jyotirjarāyū rajaso vimāne | imam apāṁ saṁgame sūryasya śiśuṁ na viprā matibhī rihanti ||
english: This Vena has set in motion the speckled-bellied one, the light-wombed, the measurer of the midspace. The inspired ones caress with their thoughts this one here, at the meeting of the waters with the sun, as they would a young child.

sanskrit: samudrād ūrmim ud iyarti veno nabhojāḥ pṛṣṭhaṁ haryatasya darśi | ṛtasya sānāv adhi viṣṭapi bhrāṭ samānaṁ yonim abhy anūṣata vrāḥ ||
english: Vena the sky-born raises a wave from the ocean; the back of the tawny one, the beloved, is seen. Shining on the peak of cosmic order, dwelling in the heights, the bands sang forth together toward the common womb.

sanskrit: samānam pūrvīr abhi vāvaśānās tiṣṭhan vatsasya mātaraḥ sanīḻāḥ | ṛtasya sānāv adhi cakramāṇā rihanti madhvo amṛtasya vāṇīḥ ||
english: Many, crying out toward the same one, they stand — the mothers of the calf, nestled together. Stepping forward on the peak of cosmic order, they lick the voices of the sweet and immortal one.

sanskrit: jānanto rūpam akṛpanta viprā mṛgasya ghoṣam mahiṣasya hi gman | ṛtena yanto adhi sindhum asthur vidad gandharvo amṛtāni nāma ||
english: The inspired ones, knowing his form, cried out; for they went toward the sound of the gazelle, of the buffalo. Going by the law of cosmic order they stood upon the stream; the Gandharva found the immortal names.

sanskrit: apsarā jāram upasiṣmiyāṇā yoṣā bibharti parame vyoman | carat priyasya yoniṣu priyaḥ san sīdat pakṣe hiraṇyaye sa venaḥ ||
english: The Apsaras, smiling at her lover, the woman, bears him in the highest heaven. Moving in the wombs of the beloved one, he who is himself beloved — that Vena sits upon the golden wing.

sanskrit: nāke suparṇam upa yat patantaṁ hṛdā venanto abhy acakṣata tvā | hiraṇyapakṣaṁ varuṇasya dūtaṁ yamasya yonau śakunam bhuraṇyum ||
english: When they beheld you flying toward the vault of heaven, with their hearts longing they gazed upon you — the golden-winged bird, messenger of Varuṇa, the active bird in the womb of Yama.

sanskrit: ūrdhvo gandharvo adhi nāke asthāt pratyaṅ citrā bibhrad asyāyudhāni | vasāno atkaṁ surabhiṁ dṛśe kaṁ sva1r ṇa nāma janata priyāṇi ||
english: The Gandharva stood upright upon the vault of heaven, carrying his variegated weapons turned outward. Wearing a fragrant garment to behold — like the sun he generated dear names.

sanskrit: drapsaḥ samudram abhi yaj jigāti paśyan gṛdhrasya cakṣasā vidharman | bhānuḥ śukreṇa śociṣā cakānas tṛtīye cakre rajasi priyāṇi ||
english: The drop that moves toward the ocean, viewing with the eagle's eye the one who holds apart — the sun, gleaming with bright radiance, placed dear things in the third sphere of the firmament.

sanskrit: imaṁ no agna upa yajñam ehi pañcayāmaṁ trivṛtaṁ saptatantum | aso havyavāḻ uta naḥ purogā jyog eva dīrghaṁ tama āśayiṣṭhāḥ ||
english: Come to this our sacrifice, O Agni — the five-staged, triple, seven-threaded. Be our carrier of oblations and our vanguard. For too long indeed you have lain in the long darkness.

sanskrit: adevād devaḥ pracatā guhā yan prapaśyamāno amṛtatvam emi | śivaṁ yat santam aśivo jahāmi svāt sakhyād araṇīṁ nābhim emi ||
english: From the non-divine I go as a god by the expansive hidden path, seeing before me immortality. That which is auspicious — though inauspicious I abandon — I go from my own friendship to a stranger-navel, a new home.

sanskrit: paśyann anyasyā atithiṁ vayāyā ṛtasya dhāma vi mime purūṇi | śaṁsāmi pitre asurāya śevam ayajñiyād yajñiyam bhāgam emi ||
english: Seeing the guest of another, the bird, I measure out the many stations of cosmic order. I declare what is beneficial to our father Asura; I go from the unworthy of sacrifice to the portion worthy of sacrifice.

sanskrit: bahvīḥ samā akaram antar asminn indraṁ vṛṇānaḥ pitaraṁ jahāmi | agniḥ somo varuṇas te cyavante paryāvard rāṣṭraṁ tad avāmy āyan ||
english: Many years I spent within this one; choosing Indra, I leave behind my father. Agni, Soma, Varuṇa — they are set in motion. That kingdom has been turned back; I seek to protect it as it comes.

sanskrit: nirmāyā u tye asurā abhūvan tvaṁ ca mā varuṇa kāmayāse | ṛtena rājann anṛtaṁ viviñcan mama rāṣṭrasyādhipatyam ehi ||
english: Those Asuras have lost their magic powers, and you, O Varuṇa, desire me. O king, separating truth from falsehood — come to sovereignty over my kingdom.

sanskrit: idaṁ svar idam id āsa vāmam ayam prakāśa urv a1ntarikṣam | hanāva vṛtraṁ nirehi soma haviṣ ṭvā santaṁ haviṣā yajāma ||
english: This is the heavenly light; this indeed was the prize; this is the illumined, the wide midspace. Let us two smite Vṛtra — come forth, O Soma! You are the oblation; we worship you who are such with oblation.

sanskrit: kaviḥ kavitvā divi rūpam āsajad aprabhūtī varuṇo nir apaḥ sṛjat | kṣemaṁ kṛṇvānā janayo na sindhavas tā asya varṇaṁ śucayo bharibhrati ||
english: The seer, by his seer-power, has fixed his form in heaven; Varuṇa, by his unobstructed might, released the waters. Like women, like rivers making a home, those shining ones continually carry his color.

sanskrit: tā asya jyeṣṭham indriyaṁ sacante tā īm ā kṣeti svadhayā madantīḥ | tā īṁ viśo na rājānaṁ vṛṇānā bībhatsuvo apa vṛtrād atiṣṭhan ||
english: They accompany his greatest power; rejoicing in their own nature they dwell with him. Choosing him as their king, as clans choose a ruler, the loathers stood away from Vṛtra.

sanskrit: bībhatsūnāṁ sayujaṁ haṁsam āhur apāṁ divyānāṁ sakhye carantam | anuṣṭubham anu carcūryamāṇam indraṁ ni cikyuḥ kavayo manīṣā ||
english: The yoke-companion of those who loathe, the swan moving in fellowship with the celestial waters — the seers knew Indra to be of anuṣṭubh meter, roaming after it, echoing it again and again, through wisdom.

sanskrit: ahaṁ rudrebhir vasubhiś carāmy aham ādityair uta viśvadevaiḥ | aham mitrāvaruṇobhā bibharmy aham indrāgnī aham aśvinobhā ||
english: I move with the Rudras and the Vasus; I move with the Ādityas and the Viśvadevas. I bear both Mitra and Varuṇa; I bear Indra and Agni, and I bear both Aśvins.

sanskrit: ahaṁ somam āhanasam bibharmy ahaṁ tvaṣṭāram uta pūṣaṇam bhagam | ahaṁ dadhāmi draviṇaṁ haviṣmate suprāvye3 yajamānāya sunvate ||
english: I bear Soma the crusher, and I bear Tvaṣṭṛ, and Pūṣan and Bhaga. I bestow wealth on the one who offers oblation, on the sacrificer who presses Soma and is worthy of aid.

sanskrit: ahaṁ rāṣṭrī saṁgamanī vasūnāṁ cikituṣī prathamā yajñiyānām | tām mā devā vy adadhuḥ purutrā bhūristhātrām bhūry āveśayantīm ||
english: I am the queen, the gatherer of treasures, the discerning one, foremost among those worthy of worship. The gods distributed me in many places — I who have many abodes, who enter into many things.

sanskrit: mayā so annam atti yo vipaśyati yaḥ prāṇiti ya īṁ śṛṇoty uktam | amantavo māṁ ta upa kṣiyanti śrudhi śruta śraddhivaṁ te vadāmi ||
english: Through me, whoever sees, whoever breathes, whoever hears what is spoken — eats food. Those who do not know me dwell beside me. Hear, O you who are heard! I speak to you what is worthy of trust.

sanskrit: aham eva svayam idaṁ vadāmi juṣṭaṁ devebhir uta mānuṣebhiḥ | yaṁ kāmaye taṁ-tam ugraṁ kṛṇomi tam brahmāṇaṁ tam ṛṣiṁ taṁ sumedhām ||
english: I alone speak this, beloved of gods and of men alike. Whomsoever I love, that very one I make mighty — I make him a brahman, a seer, a person of great wisdom.

sanskrit: ahaṁ rudrāya dhanur ā tanomi brahmadviṣe śarave hantavā u | ahaṁ janāya samadaṁ kṛṇomy ahaṁ dyāvāpṛthivī ā viveśa ||
english: I stretch the bow for Rudra, that his arrow may slay the hater of sacred knowledge. I make battle for the people; I have entered into heaven and earth.

sanskrit: ahaṁ suve pitaram asya mūrdhan mama yonir apsv antaḥ samudre | tato vi tiṣṭhe bhuvanānu viśvotāmūṁ dyāṁ varṣmaṇopa spṛśāmi ||
english: I give birth to the father of this world upon its summit. My womb is in the waters, within the ocean. From there I spread through all the worlds, and with my greatness I touch yonder sky.

sanskrit: aham eva vāta iva pra vāmy ārabhamāṇā bhuvanāni viśvā | paro divā para enā pṛthivyaitāvatī mahinā sam babhūva ||
english: I myself blow like the wind, embracing all the worlds. Beyond the sky and beyond this earth — such is my greatness; I have become.

sanskrit: na tam aṁho na duritaṁ devāso aṣṭa martyam | sajoṣaso yam aryamā mitro nayanti varuṇo ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: No distress, no sin has touched that mortal, O gods, whom Aryaman, Mitra and Varuṇa lead in agreement past his enemies.

sanskrit: tad dhi vayaṁ vṛṇīmahe varuṇa mitrāryaman | yenā nir aṁhaso yūyam pātha nethā ca martyam ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: For that very thing we choose you, O Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman — by which you guard and lead the mortal free from distress, past his enemies.

sanskrit: te nūnaṁ no 'yam ūtaye varuṇo mitro aryamā | nayiṣṭhā u no neṣaṇi parṣiṣṭhā u naḥ parṣaṇy ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: May those — Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman — now come here for our aid. The most skilled guides shall guide us on our going; the best ferriers shall ferry us across, past our enemies.

sanskrit: yūyaṁ viśvam pari pātha varuṇo mitro aryamā | yuṣmākaṁ śarmaṇi priye syāma supraṇītayo 'ti dviṣaḥ ||
english: You protect the whole world — Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman. May we be in your dear shelter, well-guided, past our enemies.

sanskrit: ādityāso ati sridho varuṇo mitro aryamā | ugram marudbhī rudraṁ huvemendram agniṁ svastaye 'ti dviṣaḥ ||
english: The Ādityas — Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman — pass beyond those who slip. We invoke fierce Rudra with the Maruts, and Indra and Agni, for our welfare, past our enemies.

sanskrit: netāra ū ṣu ṇas tiro varuṇo mitro aryamā | ati viśvāni duritā rājānaś carṣaṇīnām ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: Be leaders then for us across — Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman — past all mishaps, kings of humankind, past our enemies.

sanskrit: śunam asmabhyam ūtaye varuṇo mitro aryamā | śarma yacchantu sapratha ādityāso yad īmahe ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: May Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, grant us abundant aid — may the Ādityas of wide renown grant shelter for what we seek, past our enemies.

sanskrit: yathā ha tyad vasavo gauryaṁ cit padi ṣitām amuñcatā yajatrāḥ | evo ṣv a1sman muñcatā vy aṁhaḥ pra tāry agne prataraṁ na āyuḥ ||
english: Just as you, O Vasus, O adorable gods, once freed even the aurochs-cow that was bound by the foot — so now release us from distress! O Agni, stretch our life forward, still farther.

sanskrit: rātrī vy akhyad āyatī purutrā devy a1kṣabhiḥ | viśvā adhi śriyo 'dhita ||
english: The divine Night, arriving, has looked forth in many places with her eyes. She has put on all glories.

sanskrit: orv aprā amartyā nivato devy u1dvataḥ | jyotiṣā bādhate tamaḥ ||
english: The immortal goddess has filled the wide depths and the heights. With her light she drives away the darkness.

sanskrit: nir u svasāram askṛtoṣasaṁ devy āyatī | aped u hāsate tamaḥ ||
english: The goddess, arriving now, has indeed sent away her sister Dawn. And now the darkness too retreats, withdrawing.

sanskrit: sā no adya yasyā vayaṁ ni te yāmann avikṣmahi | vṛkṣe na vasatiṁ vayaḥ ||
english: She, at whose passage today we have settled down as birds settle into a tree to their dwelling — to that one be propitious to us.

sanskrit: ni grāmāso avikṣata ni padvanto ni pakṣiṇaḥ | ni śyenāsaś cid arthinaḥ ||
english: The villages have settled down, the creatures with feet have settled, and so too the birds — even the eagles, intent on their prey.

sanskrit: yāvayā vṛkya1ṁ vṛkaṁ yavaya stenam ūrmye | athā naḥ sutarā bhava ||
english: Keep away the she-wolf and the wolf, keep away the thief, O Ūrmī — and then be easy for us to pass through.

sanskrit: upa mā pepiśat tamaḥ kṛṣṇaṁ vyaktam asthita | uṣa ṛṇeva yātaya ||
english: The darkness, thick and palpable, has crept up and enveloped me. O Dawn, like a debt, make it pay and depart.

sanskrit: upa te gā ivākaraṁ vṛṇīṣva duhitar divaḥ | rātri stomaṁ na jigyuṣe ||
english: I have approached you as cattle approach — accept it, O daughter of heaven; receive this praise-song, O Night, as one who has won the prize.

sanskrit: mamāgne varco vihaveṣv astu vayaṁ tvendhānās tanvam puṣema | mahyaṁ namantām pradiśaś catasras tvayādhyakṣeṇa pṛtanā jayema ||
english: May my brilliance be present, O Agni, in the manifold invocations; kindling you, may we nourish our bodies. May the four quarters bow down to me; with you as our overlord, may we conquer in battles.

sanskrit: mama devā vihave santu sarva indravanto maruto viṣṇur agniḥ | mamāntarikṣam urulokam astu mahyaṁ vātaḥ pavatāṁ kāme asmin ||
english: May all the gods be in my invocation — the Maruts with Indra, Viṣṇu, and Agni. May the midspace and the wide realm be mine; may the wind blow for me in this desire.

sanskrit: mayi devā draviṇam ā yajantām mayy āśīr astu mayi devahūtiḥ | daivyā hotāro vanuṣanta pūrve 'riṣṭāḥ syāma tanvā suvīrāḥ ||
english: May the gods sacrifice wealth into me; may blessing be upon me, may the invocation of the gods be upon me. The divine hotars of old sought to win — may we be unharmed in body and rich in heroic sons.

sanskrit: mahyaṁ yajantu mama yāni havyākūtiḥ satyā manaso me astu | eno mā ni gāṁ katamac canāhaṁ viśve devāso adhi vocatā naḥ ||
english: Let them sacrifice for me; may the intent of my oblation be true to my mind's purpose. May I not fall into any sin whatever — let all you gods speak in my behalf.

sanskrit: devīḥ ṣaḻ urvīr uru naḥ kṛṇota viśve devāsa iha vīrayadhvam | mā hāsmahi prajayā mā tanūbhir mā radhāma dviṣate soma rājan ||
english: Make the six divine spacious realms wide for us; all you gods, show your heroic power here! May we not lose progeny or bodies; may we not fall into the power of him who hates us, O King Soma.

sanskrit: agne manyum pratinudan pareṣām adabdho gopāḥ pari pāhi nas tvam | pratyañco yantu nigutaḥ punas te3 'maiṣāṁ cittam prabudhāṁ vi neśat ||
english: O Agni, warding off the fury of our enemies, inviolable guardian, protect us! May their hidden foes go back again; may their wakened thought come to naught.

sanskrit: dhātā dhātṝṇām bhuvanasya yas patir devaṁ trātāram abhimātiṣāham | imaṁ yajñam aśvinobhā bṛhaspatir devāḥ pāntu yajamānaṁ nyarthāt ||
english: May Dhātṛ the establisher, lord of the world, the divine protector who overcomes assailants — may both Aśvins, Bṛhaspati, and the gods guard this sacrifice and the sacrificer from harm.

sanskrit: uruvyacā no mahiṣaḥ śarma yaṁsad asmin have puruhūtaḥ purukṣuḥ | sa naḥ prajāyai haryaśva mṛḻayendra mā no rīriṣo mā parā dāḥ ||
english: May the great bull of wide reach grant us shelter in this invocation — the much-invoked, the much-possessing one. O Indra of the bay steeds, be merciful to us for our progeny; do not harm us, do not abandon us.

sanskrit: ye naḥ sapatnā apa te bhavantv indrāgnibhyām ava bādhāmahe tān | vasavo rudrā ādityā uparispṛśam mograṁ cettāram adhirājam akran ||
english: Let our rivals be away from us; we press them down with Indra and Agni. The Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas have made the fierce, all-knowing overlord to reach on high.

sanskrit: nāsad āsīn no sad āsīt tadānīṁ nāsīd rajo no vyomā paro yat | kim āvarīvaḥ kuha kasya śarmann ambhaḥ kim āsīd gahanaṁ gabhīram ||
english: Then was neither non-being nor being; there was neither the realm of space nor the sky beyond. What stirred? Where? In whose shelter? Was there water, the deep and unfathomable?

sanskrit: na mṛtyur āsīd amṛtaṁ na tarhi na rātryā ahna āsīt praketaḥ | ānīd avātaṁ svadhayā tad ekaṁ tasmād dhānyan na paraḥ kiṁ canāsa ||
english: Death was not then, nor immortality; no signal was there of night and day. That One breathed, windless, by its own power; other than that, nothing whatsoever existed.

sanskrit: tama āsīt tamasā gūḻham agre 'praketaṁ salilaṁ sarvam ā idam | tucchyenābhv apihitaṁ yad āsīt tapasas tan mahinājāyataikam ||
english: Darkness was hidden by darkness in the beginning; all this was undifferentiated water. The life-force that was covered with emptiness — that One arose through the power of heat.

sanskrit: kāmas tad agre sam avartatādhi manaso retaḥ prathamaṁ yad āsīt | sato bandhum asati nir avindan hṛdi pratīṣyā kavayo manīṣā ||
english: Desire came upon That One in the beginning — that which was the primal seed, born of the mind. The seers, searching within their hearts with wisdom, found the bond of being in non-being.

sanskrit: tiraścīno vitato raśmir eṣām adhaḥ svid āsī3d upari svid āsī3t | retodhā āsan mahimāna āsan svadhā avastāt prayatiḥ parastāt ||
english: Their cord was stretched across — was it below? Was it above? There were seed-placers; there were powers. Self-sufficiency below, impulse above.

sanskrit: ko addhā veda ka iha pra vocat kuta ājātā kuta iyaṁ visṛṣṭiḥ | arvāg devā asya visarjanenāthā ko veda yata ābabhūva ||
english: Who truly knows? Who here shall proclaim it? Whence was it born? Whence came this creation? The gods came after the creation of this world — who then knows from where it arose?

sanskrit: iyaṁ visṛṣṭir yata ābabhūva yadi vā dadhe yadi vā na | yo asyādhyakṣaḥ parame vyoman so aṅga veda yadi vā na veda ||
english: He from whom this creation arose — whether he made it or whether he did not — he who is its overseer in the highest heaven, he alone knows — or perhaps he does not know.

sanskrit: yo yajño viśvatas tantubhis tata ekaśataṁ devakarmebhir āyataḥ | ime vayanti pitaro ya āyayuḥ pra vayāpa vayety āsate tate ||
english: The sacrifice that was spread on all sides with threads — the one-hundred-and-one, extended by the acts of the gods — these fathers who came as weavers now sit weaving at the web, crying 'Weave on, weave on.'

sanskrit: pumām enaṁ tanuta ut kṛṇatti pumān vi tatne adhi nāke asmin | ime mayūkhā upa sedur ū sadaḥ sāmāni cakrus tasarāṇy otave ||
english: A man extends it; a man cuts it up; a man has spread it out upon this vault of heaven. These pegs have taken their seat together — they have made the sāmans the shuttle-bobbins for the weaving.

sanskrit: kāsīt pramā pratimā kiṁ nidānam ājyaṁ kim āsīt paridhiḥ ka āsīt | chandaḥ kim āsīt praügaṁ kim ukthaṁ yad devā devam ayajanta viśve ||
english: What was the measure? What was the model? What was the fastening? What was the ghee? What was the enclosure? What was the meter? What was the introductory chant? What was the recitation — when all the gods sacrificed to the god?

sanskrit: agner gāyatry abhavat sayugvoṣṇihayā savitā sam babhūva | anuṣṭubhā soma ukthair mahasvān bṛhaspater bṛhatī vācam āvat ||
english: Agni was joined to the Gāyatrī; Savitṛ came together with the Uṣṇih meter; Soma, great with anuṣṭubh recitations, was yoked to them; Bṛhaspati's Bṛhatī covered speech.

sanskrit: virāṇ mitrāvaruṇayor abhiśrīr indrasya triṣṭub iha bhāgo ahnaḥ | viśvān devāñ jagaty ā viveśa tena cākḷpra ṛṣayo manuṣyāḥ ||
english: The Virāj is the glory of Mitra and Varuṇa; the Triṣṭubh is Indra's portion of the day here. The Jagatī entered into all the gods; with that the seers and human beings were made fit.

sanskrit: cākḷpre tena ṛṣayo manuṣyā yajñe jāte pitaro naḥ purāṇe | paśyan manye manasā cakṣasā tān ya imaṁ yajñam ayajanta pūrve ||
english: The seers and human beings were made fit by that, when the sacrifice was born, our fathers of old. With the mind's eye, I think I see those who first performed this sacrifice.

sanskrit: sahastomāḥ sahachandasa āvṛtaḥ sahapramā ṛṣayaḥ sapta daivyāḥ | pūrveṣām panthām anudṛśya dhīrā anvālebhire rathyo3 na raśmīn ||
english: Together with the praise-songs, together with the meters bound together, together with the measures — the seven divine seers. The wise ones, looking back along the path of the ancients, grasped the reins like chariot-drivers.
